sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This very ability to receive nurture through two opposite modes depends on a person's divine service.

translations.translation: Now, this very matter—that they can receive nurture through these two modes—
depends on the service of man.
For it is written,
"Yaakov is the rope of His inheritance."
As a parable,
a rope whose one end is tied above and the other end below—
when the lower end is moved, the upper end also moves.
And so it is in the service of the souls of Israel,
that according to the manner of man's service below, so it is made above.
That is, when a person lowers himself into material things,
instead of his inner will being for G-dliness in Torah and prayer,
he lowers himself into material things,
thereby causing above an increase of tzimtzumim until nurture for the external forces can come from this.
And likewise, when a person elevates himself in a manner of haughtiness and arrogance,
even though he knows well his own lowliness,
nevertheless he elevates himself without reason or knowledge,
then "spirit brings spirit,"
causing nurture for the external forces from a very high place.
And this is the matter of Pharaoh, the letters of "the back of the neck" (HaOref),
who receives from the aspect of the back of the neck of Arich,
which is a very high level,
and this matter depends on service,
that when "they turned to Me their back and not their face"
(as stated in the Haftarah),
then through this the aspect of Pharaoh is drawn, who nurses from the back of the neck of Arich Anpin,
where "as the darkness, so is the light," etc.
And this is the matter of the double-edged sword,
to cut off their nurture from both modes.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: In the detailed explanation, the three ministers of Pharaoh correspond to the throat's structures and their counterparts in holiness.

translations.translation: D)
And to understand the matter in detail,
it is explained in the books of Kabbalah and Chassidus, in the discourses on Egypt and the Exodus from Egypt,
that Egypt (Mitzrayim) is the straits of the throat,
for in the throat there are three aspects,
the windpipe, the esophagus, and the jugular veins,
which are the three ministers of Pharaoh,
the chief cupbearer, the chief butcher, and the chief baker.
And behold,
just as there is Egypt and the three ministers of Pharaoh in the side of impurity,
so too there is Egypt and the three ministers in holiness.
For the chief cupbearer is the drawing down of pleasure,
since water causes all kinds of pleasure to grow,
and this is the matter of drawing down the Divine pleasure throughout the entire order of the chain of descent.
And in the human body, this is the windpipe,
for in the windpipe there are the nerves of the brain, and through the nerves, pleasure is drawn from the brain throughout the entire body,
as our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"There are three windpipes; one branches to the heart, one branches to the lungs, and one branches to the liver,"
which are the general organs,
and this is the aspect of the windpipe, which draws pleasure from the brain through the nerves of the brain throughout the entire body.
And in service, this is the study of Torah with pleasure,
for pleasure is the inwardness of the Torah,
and likewise, pleasure in prayer,
this is the aspect of the chief cupbearer.
And the chief butcher in service is the matter of the boiling of the blood in holiness,
which is the aspect of love like flames of fire,
for the chief cupbearer is the aspect of love with pleasures, which is love drawn like water,
and the chief butcher is love like flames of fire.
And the chief baker is Torah,
and this is so even though it was stated above that the chief cupbearer is Torah,
for that is the pleasure of Torah,
but Torah in general is the matter of the chief baker,
for Torah is called "wheat" (Chitah),
numerically equivalent to twenty-two,
the twenty-two letters of the Torah,
and from the wheat one must make bread,
as it is written,
"Come, eat of my bread,"
and in order for the wheat to become bread, this is through baking,
as it is written,
"And ten women shall bake your bread in one oven,"
where the oven is the heat of love like flames of fire,
and "one" is the Unique One of the world,
and "one oven" means the heat and flames of fire in the matter of the Unique One of the world,
thus there are two matters here,
the matter of the oven, which is the flames of fire,
and the matter of the Unique One of the world, which is most sublime,
and this is the aspect of the chief baker, which is the Torah,
which is the intermediary between the two lines of the chief cupbearer and the chief butcher.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: These three ministers in holiness cut off the vitality from the three ministers of Pharaoh in the side of impurity.

translations.translation: And these three ministers in holiness cut off the vitality from the three ministers of the side of impurity.
For behold, also in the side of impurity there are three ministers of Pharaoh,
the chief cupbearer in the side of impurity is pleasure in material matters,
for even though it is the desire for that which is permitted,
nevertheless,
one who is immersed in them causes that he is not at all connected to a G-dly matter.
And the chief butcher is the boiling of the blood in material things and also in physical things.
And the chief baker is that his entire matter is not invested in Torah but in physicality.
And through the three ministers as they are in holiness, they cut off the nurture from the three ministers of Pharaoh of the side of impurity.
For behold,
through the chief cupbearer in holiness, which is the service of love with pleasures,
whose matter is the drawing down of pleasure in the chain of descent through the Sefirah of Chochmah,
which is the aspect of the windpipe,
"Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding,"
behold, through this he cuts off the nurture that they nurse from a high place,
for when the drawing down is through Chochmah, whose matter is self-nullification,
then they are unable to receive,
because,
what they nurse from the high place,
this is only when it is in the aspect of the encompassing light specifically,
but when it is drawn down internally,
then they are unable to nurse,
as is explained in Kuntres U'Mayan
at length.
And this is the matter of the chief cupbearer, who cuts off the nurture from the high place.
And through the chief butcher in holiness, he cuts off the nurture from the multitude of tzimtzumim,
which is caused by a person lowering himself into material things,
and this is that through the love like flames of fire and the boiling of the blood in holiness,
the boiling of the blood in the side of impurity is consumed,
which is what the Targum translates for the verse "chief butcher"
as "Rav Katulya" (chief slaughterer),
whose matter is as stated in the Gemara
on the verse,
"He who offers a sacrifice of thanksgiving honors Me,"
"Whoever slaughters his evil inclination," etc.,
meaning that through the boiling of the blood in holiness, he consumes the boiling of the blood in the side of impurity,
and consequently the nurture from the aspect of the multitude of tzimtzumim is nullified.
